parsed.rationale: Both `StreamingLinkTapped.init(service:artist:album:)` (line 56) and `ExternalLinkTapped.init(service:artist:album:)` (line 70) are flagged as exact function duplicates sharing the identical signature `init(service:artist:album:)` within the same file `Shared/Analytics/Sources/Analytics/Events/UIEvents.swift` in the `Analytics` package. Because they are co-located in one file and represent distinct named event types, neither a cross-package extraction nor a generic collapse is appropriate. The duplication is best resolved by extracting the shared initializer body into a private helper or a protocol with a default implementation scoped to this file, eliminating the maintenance risk of the two bodies diverging silently.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a shared private or internal helper initializer (or a common base struct/protocol with a default implementation) within `Shared/Analytics/Sources/Analytics/Events/UIEvents.swift` in the `Analytics` package that captures the duplicated `init(service:artist:album:)` body. Both `StreamingLinkTapped` and `ExternalLinkTapped` can then delegate to this shared logic — either via a protocol with a default implementation in an extension, or by extracting the shared parameter-mapping logic into a private free function in the same file that both initializers call.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Both initializers live in the same file (`Shared/Analytics/Sources/Analytics/Events/UIEvents.swift`) and the same package (`Analytics`), so `extract-to-common` (which targets a different upstream package) is not the right framing. `default-implementation` requires a named protocol that already exists in the cluster's source files, and none is named in the cluster row. `generic-parameterization` would require the two types to be collapsible into a single generic type, but they are distinct domain event types (`StreamingLinkTapped` vs `ExternalLinkTapped`) whose semantic difference is intentional — collapsing them would lose type-level event discrimination. The most idiomatic Swift fix is a same-file private helper or a protocol extension, which does not map cleanly to any single named category.
